{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-id-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"c9af1abf2940fe9ab53d1a3ae852c5102a71da979458e6f77888e24bde1eee79","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-id-class-d:lineage:50","source_registry_sha256":"9c432577e712960022ff656d6738a091319c6e5e4dcbdcf9429cd450e142e543","source_liveness_sha256":"eee60602368bd429216c9c2833be0be6ed9e505e5c5accebaefb9d2b9a847475"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Defensive driving, attention and fatigue","heading":"C2 — Defensive driving, attention and fatigue","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Defensive driving, attention and fatigue

FACT_ID: sec11-R01 | anchor: A91
Safe driving requires continuous attention so changes can be seen and answered in time. [A91]
Source: [A91 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec11-R02 | anchor: A91
Talking on a phone or texting can distract a driver and contribute to a crash. [A91]
Source: [A91 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec11-R03 | anchor: A91
Eating, reading or writing while driving can divert attention from the road. [A91]
Source: [A91 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec11-R04 | anchor: A91
Changing radio settings or lighting a cigarette can distract from driving. [A91]
Source: [A91 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec11-R05 | anchor: A91
Applying makeup or shaving can distract the driver. [A91]
Source: [A91 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec11-R06 | anchor: A91
Searching inside the vehicle or dealing with children or pets can draw attention away from driving. [A91]
Source: [A91 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec11-R07 | anchor: A91
Even a few seconds of distraction can hide a child entering from between parked cars, a cyclist crossing the path or sudden braking ahead. [A91]
Source: [A91 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec11-R08 | anchor: A92
Preset radio stations and load recorded audio before driving. [A92]
Source: [A92 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec11-R09 | anchor: A92
Keep audio low enough to hear outside warnings, including sirens, horns and tire noise. [A92]
Source: [A92 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec11-R10 | anchor: A92
A front-seat passenger can handle navigation from maps or a phone; a solo driver should learn the route before entering the vehicle. [A92]
Source: [A92 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec11-R11 | anchor: A92
Do not eat while driving. [A92]
Source: [A92 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec11-R12 | anchor: A92
Teach children appropriate in-car behavior so tending them does not take attention from the road. [A92]
Source: [A92 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec11-R13 | anchor: A92
Use a pet carrier to prevent pets from causing problems during the drive. [A92]
Source: [A92 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec11-R14 | anchor: A92
If lost in thought and inattentive, pull to the roadside and stop for a break. [A92]
Source: [A92 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec11-R15 | anchor: A93
Park in a safe place before making a phone call or exchanging text messages. [A93]
Source: [A93 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec11-R16 | anchor: A93
When drowsy, stop driving, leave the highway at the first rest stop or service area and take a nap. [A93]
Source: [A93 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec11-R17 | anchor: A93
Do not depend on stimulants or energy drinks to keep driving while sleepy; the handbook warns they can increase danger. [A93]
Source: [A93 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec11-R18 | anchor: A93
Highway hypnosis is drowsiness associated with monotony and the steady noise of wind and tires. [A93]
Source: [A93 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec11-R19 | anchor: A93
On long drives, shift visual attention among roadway areas and objects at differing distances and to both sides. [A93]
Source: [A93 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec11-R20 | anchor: A93
An unattended vehicle in a highway's traveled portion may be towed immediately at any time. [A93]
Source: [A93 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec11-R21 | anchor: A93
An unattended vehicle off the traveled lanes but on the highway's paved portion must be removed before dark or may be towed at the owner's expense. [A93]
Source: [A93 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec11-R22 | anchor: A94
The handbook describes Alive at 25 as a defensive-driving course for ages fifteen through twenty-four. [A94]
Source: [A94 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec11-R23 | anchor: A94
Law enforcement presents the described course's responsible-choice strategies for young people driving or riding as passengers. [A94]
Source: [A94 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0094]
